title: Japan Air Lines Flight 123
subtitle: Tokyo Haneda → Osaka Itami
note: A reconstruction of a real accident in which 520 people died. It ends before the impact.
summary: A Boeing 747SR-46 on a domestic flight from Tokyo Haneda to Osaka Itami, with 509 passengers and 15 crew aboard.
At 18:24:35, twelve minutes after take-off, the aft pressure bulkhead failed at 23,900 ft off the east coast of the Izu Peninsula. Most of the fin and all four hydraulic systems were lost.
For 32 minutes the crew kept the aircraft flying, steering with engine thrust: over Suruga Bay, west of Mt Fuji, in a loop near Otsuki, then over Okutama and the mountains to the north-west.
At 18:56 the aircraft struck the Osutaka Ridge in Ueno Village, Gunma. 520 people died. Four survived.

crew.name: Yutaka Sasaki
crew.detail: flying from the left seat, in captain training

card.title: Japan Air Lines Flight 123
lines: 12 August 1985 · Boeing 747SR-46 JA8119, Tokyo Haneda to Osaka Itami.
At 18:56 the aircraft struck the Osutaka Ridge in Ueno Village, Gunma. Of the 524 people aboard, 509 passengers and 15 crew, 520 died. Four survived.
The crew kept the aircraft flying for 32 minutes after its aft pressure bulkhead failed and took all four hydraulic systems with it.
Every 12 August families and JAL staff climb to the ridge; a moment of silence is held at 18:56.
JAL's Safety Promotion Center at Haneda keeps the wreckage and the lessons of this accident.
Reconstruction from the official report of the Aircraft Accident Investigation Commission (1987).
